# Content Editor Provenance Panel

> Source: `specs/workbench/2.3-content-editor-provenance.md`
> Parent: `knowledge-ops-workbench-ux-breakdown.md`
> Points: 1

**Parent**: `knowledge-ops-workbench-ux-breakdown.md`
**Epic**: 2. Content Editor View
**Points**: 1
**Dependencies**: 2.1 Content Editor Shell, P1B (graph memory for provenance data)

## Purpose

Right panel showing sources, agent contributions, and corrections that shaped the document.

## Scope

Breakdown 2026-05-29: Code inspection confirms 2.1 shell dependency is satisfied — ContentEditorPage.tsx and DocumentFields.tsx both exist in frontend/src/. ProvenancePanel.tsx does not yet exist; MemorySignalChip.tsx exists and can be reused for memory strength display. editor-types.ts needs a ProvenanceData interface added. P1B (graph memory) is status: ready (not done), but is not a hard blocker: the entire editor layer uses mock data (MOCK_DOCUMENT pattern), and acceptance tests require only UI rendering of provenance fields, not a live graph API. Work is bounded to 2 files. Points: 1sp. DoD: (1) frontend/src/components/editor/ProvenancePanel.tsx created and renders Sources, Agent, Corrections, Memory Node sections with mock data; (2) Expand in Memory link navigates to /workbench/memory; (3) Component mounted in ContentEditorPage aside sidebar next to DocumentFields; (4) pnpm typecheck passes in frontend/; (5) pnpm test passes in frontend/. Verdict: ready — all 4 gate checks pass: 1sp ≤5sp, DoD is concrete (named files + CLI commands), no hard inter-task dependency blocking (2.1 done, P1B UI-only mock acceptable), zero ambiguity on exit signal. --tasks-dir orgs/open-hax/openplanner/packages/agents/knoxx/kanban

## Proposed current-source refinement — issue #158, 2026-10-07

This adds a reviewable plan to the EXISTING whole card. Original UUID, Ready / P2 / 1, creation time, source and parent body routing are unchanged, and all five original outcomes remain obligations. Native Ready is observed lifecycle visibility; eligible planning admission for this refinement is not yet demonstrated. No lifecycle, dependency field, event or estimate is edited. The earlier one-point/two-file placement is historical and must be reconsidered against current source without silently changing scope.

### Context and outcome

Accepted origin `3409977bca4ba35e09967f9a99d50867a679a73c` retains ContentEditorPage.tsx, DocumentFields and the mock document, but actual Shadow-owned app routing and its React bridge do not mount/export that editor. Its migration record is legacy/port. The requested provenance panel is absent. Merely adding a disconnected legacy component would not deliver a user-visible editor sidebar. Existing `/workbench/memory` also falls through the current wildcard route rather than a memory view.

Deliver the complete mock provenance sidebar on an actually mounted, protected editor route, beside the existing document fields. Show Sources, Agent, Corrections and Memory Node, preserve the accepted document/edit/publish controls, and make Expand in Memory navigate to the original requested path with a reviewed real destination rather than silently falling back home. Mock attribution is visibly mock data, never proof of an actual actor, event, source admission or memory promotion. No live graph dependency is introduced.

### Scope, boundary and proposed placement

Prefer the smallest reviewed integration: keep the already-permitted frontend React/TSX editor and DocumentFields, add the provenance UI using the existing canonical Uxx React primitives/MemorySignalChip, and expose the editor through the current bridge and protected CLJS router. The exact editor path/entry control and `/workbench/memory` mapping require review against current CMS/migration ownership; a possible alias to the existing protected `/ops/vectors` surface is a proposal, not accepted equivalence to every memory feature. If that destination cannot satisfy the original navigation intent, retain the hold rather than implement a bogus redirect. Full CLJS editor migration is an alternative requiring explicit scope/size/owner review, not an excuse to narrow criteria or to build a second UI kit.

Keep any reusable pure fixture normalization/shape/display decisions portable `.cljc` where practical; represent mock provenance as plain data. React props/type mirrors and DOM/navigation remain frontend adapters. Consume existing Uxx exports and design tokens; preserve one React/router context and the established bridge, without importing a second compiled CLJS runtime or inventing package exports. Do not expand backend TypeScript or change OpenPlanner/Uxx source. Review input validation, escaped text, unknown/empty provenance and controlled memory-signal vocabulary without turning UI fixtures into durable provenance authority.

### Acceptance criteria — all original five retained

1. Render all four original sections with deterministic, explicitly mock fixture data. Preserve source order/identities, agent contribution and correction text, memory node/signals; handle empty/missing optional data visibly and reject unsupported shape at the view-data boundary. Reuse canonical Uxx UI and existing MemorySignalChip behavior; no fabricated live provenance or unsafe raw markup.
2. Expand in Memory performs the original `/workbench/memory` navigation through the actual application router to the reviewed memory destination, preserving the intended node context if the existing destination supports it. Prove no wildcard-to-home success, unauthorized bypass, full page reload or new live provider call. Missing destination is a qualification hold, not a silently removed control.
3. Mount the panel alongside DocumentFields in the actually served editor, with a discoverable reviewed entry and protected deep-link route. Preserve the existing document editing, unsaved/save, review/publish, fields and route authorization behavior. Tests must instantiate the real application composition/bridge, not only render an isolated fixture widget. Migration inventory and overlap decisions must describe the actual mount.
4. `pnpm -C frontend typecheck` passes at the implementation head with no introduced/touched warning/error. Existing unrelated failures remain visible with owner evidence; no file exclusion, assertion weakening or return-code-only compiler qualification.
5. `pnpm -C frontend test` passes with existing tests retained and meaningful new section/mount/navigation/refusal regressions. Actual selectors must run the new tests. Also pass the owning touched CLJS, bridge/build, coverage, migration/ratchet and deterministic CI gates, and the required browser/human artifact. Deliberately failing selected assertions must make the official test command nonzero.

### Verification, ownership and holds

Design `docs/notes/design/content-editor-provenance-planning.md` specifies red/green, route/data negative controls and future seeded checkout-bound browser tour. Do not run a backend/provider/PM2 or real graph for this planning refinement. Future real verification must identify the exact served candidate and preserve missing-precondition/refusal evidence; offline unit mocks do not count as served-route proof.

The original parent is the existing workbench UX breakdown; native parent Done is provenance, not this head's review approval. Graph-memory smoke is currently native Review (the historical body said Ready); its live completion is not a hard dependency for this card's explicitly mock-only outcome. Preserve body routing, and do not invent hard UUID edges. Foreign #363 changes editor tests/CMS interaction and #369 changes the app bridge/migration surface; coordinate exact heads/ownership before code or merge, adopt neither pending branch. Parent personal sync PR1 remains pending; existing #134, #385 and zero-warning #181/#182 holds are not waived. Root is the sole publisher and request coordinator. Review must decide whether the full mount/navigation/adapter/test/human outcome still fits one point; if not, propose lawful re-estimation/breakdown without changing this metadata now. No new card, implementation or readiness uplift is supplied.


### Existing author-walkthrough admission hold

Root independently reports that canonical [author-walkthrough classification issue #22](https://github.com/riatzukiza/.agents/issues/22) remains a current qualification prerequisite: personal Knoxx #9 at `5a4c40dc71df7e1bed4e857c8f5b85ee469ebdd3`, native author review `5438887085`, has three explanatory threads which strict hosted run `37586270393` / job `112676997045` counts unresolved, failing despite successful App prerequisite steps. This is an attributed root observation, not an independently rerun provider/gate by this lane. Preserve author annotations and the actual strict failure; no self-Handled replies, local classifier, gate waiver or approval credit. Keep future publication and annotations DRAFT / blocked until the existing owner seam is corrected. This is an existing issue reference, not a new card or dependency/frontmatter change; complete required-command failure remains a hold.
